reuse.why: Builds on getDateWithSkippedWeekend, recurConfigToRSchedule and getNextDate, introduces shared predicates (skipsWeekendOccurrences, isNonWorkingDay) and routes the schedule-template.ts path through them too.

duplication.why: The 'daily skips, others move, off leaves as is' composition is rebuilt by hand in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template.ts, and firstWeekdayOccurrence/lastWeekdayOccurrence are near-identical loops.

placement.why: Day classification and the frequency rule live in shared/schedules.ts and parseRecurDate carries the new fields; the per-occurrence resolution still sits in each caller rather than in that shared module.

scope.why: Changes stay within schedule date resolution, the new handler, the RecurConfig type, tests and release notes.

maintainability.why: Predicates are named and shared, but a future change to how an occurrence is resolved must be applied consistently in four call-site compositions.

disguised_duplication.where: the skip-or-move decision is reshaped differently per caller: resolveDate/isSkippedOccurrence closures in schedule-template.ts, an if/else push loop in getUpcomingDates, a continue/else-if loop in getDatesInRange and the skipsDailyWeekends guard in getNextDate; firstWeekdayOccurrence and lastWeekdayOccurrence differ only by reverse

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains holidays; the daily special case is kept outside it and re-composed at getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and createScheduleList
